chunks: Hafs narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

‘Isa (peace be upon him) said: The provision of the world has become difficult, and the provision of the Hereafter [is also difficult]. As for the provision of the world, you do not extend your hand to anything from it except that you find an immoral person who has preceded you to it. And as for the provision of the Hereafter, you do not find helpers who assist you in it.

key_terms.الآخِرَةِ: The Hereafter, the life to come
key_terms.مَئُونَةُ: Provision, sustenance, or means of livelihood

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa say about the difficulty of worldly and hereafter provisions?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Prophet ‘Isa (peace be upon him) contrasts the external competition for worldly sustenance, where the unrighteous often seize resources first, with the internal struggle of the Hereafter, where one finds no external allies and must rely solely on personal spiritual preparation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on self-accounting (muhasabah) and the solitary nature of the individual’s standing before God, devoid of intercessors or helpers in the final reckoning.

en.hubeali: H 14560 – Hafs, who has reported the following: Abu Abdullahasws has narrated that

‘Isa<sup>as</sup> said: ‘It is intensely difficult to collect the provisions of the world and the provisions of the Hereafter, As for the provisions of the world, so you will not extend your hand towards something except that you will find an immoral one has preceded you for it, and as for the provisions of the Hereafter, so you will not find any helper who will help you for it’.
